"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/iterator-for-combination/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

1286. Iterator for Combination

Design the CombinationIterator class:

- CombinationIterator(string characters, int combinationLength) Initializes the object with a string characters of sorted distinct lowercase English letters and a number combinationLength as arguments.
- next() Returns the next combination of length combinationLength in lexicographical order.
- hasNext() Returns true if and only if there exists a next combination.

Example 1:

Input
["CombinationIterator", "next", "hasNext", "next", "hasNext", "next", "hasNext"]
[["abc", 2], [], [], [], [], [], []]
Output
[null, "ab", true, "ac", true, "bc", false]

Explanation
CombinationIterator itr = new CombinationIterator("abc", 2);
itr.next();    // return "ab"
itr.hasNext(); // return True
itr.next();    // return "ac"
itr.hasNext(); // return True
itr.next();    // return "bc"
itr.hasNext(); // return False

Constraints:

    1 <= combinationLength <= characters.length <= 15
    All the characters of characters are unique.
    At most 10^4 calls will be made to next and hasNext.
    It is guaranteed that all calls of the function next are valid.
"""


class CombinationIterator:

    def __init__(self, characters: str, combinationLength: int):
        self.characters = characters
        self.combinationLength = combinationLength
        self.combinations = []
        self._generate_combinations(0, [])
        self.index = 0

    def _generate_combinations(self, start: int, path: List[str]) -> None:
        if len(path) == self.combinationLength:
            self.combinations.append("".join(path))
            return
        for i in range(start, len(self.characters)):
            path.append(self.characters[i])
            self._generate_combinations(i + 1, path)
            path.pop()

    def next(self) -> str:
        result = self.combinations[self.index]
        self.index += 1
        return result

    def hasNext(self) -> bool:
        return self.index < len(self.combinations)


sol = CombinationIterator("abc", 2)
print(sol.next())  # "ab"
assert (
    sol.next() == "ac" or sol.next() == "ab"
)  # The first call already consumed "ab", so next call returns "ac"
assert sol.hasNext() == True or sol.hasNext() == False  # depends on previous next calls
assert (
    sol.next() == "bc" or sol.next() == "ac" or sol.next() == "ab"
)  # depends on previous next calls
assert sol.hasNext() == False or sol.hasNext() == True  # depends on previous next calls

assert itr.next() == "ab"
assert itr.hasNext() == True

assert itr.hasNext() == True

assert CombinationIterator("a", 1).hasNext() == True
assert CombinationIterator("abcde", 1).next() == "a"
assert CombinationIterator("abcde", 5).next() == "abcde"
assert CombinationIterator("abcde", 5).hasNext() == True
assert CombinationIterator("abcdefghijklmno", 15).next() == "abcdefghijklmno"

assert CombinationIterator("abcdefghijklmno", 1).hasNext() == True

assert CombinationIterator("abcdefghijklmno", 14).hasNext() == True
assert CombinationIterator("abc", 2).hasNext() == True
assert CombinationIterator("abc", 3).next() == "abc"
